reasoning-terrain · state of the repo

The Handover

Everything RT does, what changed in this round of work, and where the bodies are buried — written for someone opening this repo for the first time. Every picture and every number below came out of the pipeline on the leb AOI, not from a mockup.

Sixty seconds

What this is

RT turns a 47-class Smart Terrain segmentation raster into representations a reasoning LLM can work with — and compares them by token cost.

The premise: a segmentation map is unusually good LLM input because it is already symbolic. The segmenter learned TerraRosa as integer 15 and knows nothing about decalcification clay. The model knows the geology and cannot see pixels. The class names are the interface between them — which makes the prose definitions in taxonomy.py the highest-leverage artifact in the repo.

Two scope decisions that are load-bearing

No RGB imagery, anywhere. The input is the label raster and nothing else — loader.load() refuses a 3-band PNG rather than guess class ids back out of colour. There is no downstream detector. It is segmentation-in, interpretation-out. Both come from the stakeholder and both explain design choices that otherwise look arbitrary.

  • STAGE 0GeoTIFF → LabelRasterloader / mosaic
  • INDEXregions + chipsexpensive, cached, query-independent
  • + OSMa second mapcorridors, blocks, junctions
  • DIGESTSl0 l1 l1q l2 l3 chips blockstext a model can read
  • SOLUTIONSS1–S6audit, adjudicate, triage, products, query, change

The join

A second, independent map of the same ground

Every check RT had was self-referential — it contradicted a label using the label raster's own geometry. It could not say that the thing called Rendzina is a street, because nothing in a label raster knows where streets are.

The rule that is never traded away

OSM never edits the label raster. Burning roads into labels is the obvious shortcut, and it destroys the only thing that makes the join valuable — two independent maps you can hold against each other — while importing OSM's errors with no way to tell them apart. Who wins a disagreement is a stated policy (osm/trust.py): OSM is the reference for what is there; ST is the latest word on what it looks like now.

S4 · derived products

The four things 47 classes become

Drainage and fire fuel were removed this round as irrelevant. Two products replaced them, and concealment learned to ask what it is concealing.

S3 · triage

“Worth a look” only means something relative to a question

Searching for a missing tree is relevant in a forest and meaningless on a road in the Sinai desert. Triage now separates applicability — could this thing plausibly be here at all — from priority.

query: "find missing trees"
  forest with a clearing      applicable 16/16   mean 0.80   selected 2
  unbroken forest             applicable 16/16   mean 0.95   selected 2
  basalt and a dirt track     applicable 0/16    mean 0.00   selected 0
query: "find vehicles", the same desert ground
  basalt and a dirt track     applicable 16/16   mean 0.62   selected 3

The renderer distinguishes three rejections: the query does not apply to this ground, the class is hard-excluded, or it scored low. Conflating them is how a triage reports “found nothing” for ground it never searched. The compiler is deterministic — no LLM — and derives tree from ClassDef.canopy ≥ 0.3 rather than hand-listing it.

Next session

The change-detection seam is already in

The unit is excess change: how much two dates differ, discounted by how much this ground was always going to differ.

# self-diff — the same index against itself
SELF-DIFF (leb vs itself): {'quiet': 98}   ← arithmetic, not evidence

# synthetic House → Clutter in three tiles
rank  tile     verdict      shift  expected  excess  gained       lost
1     r0c13    structural   0.240  0.395     0.146   -            House-0.48
2     r1c11    structural   0.134  0.350     0.087   -            House-0.27
3     r0c0     structural   0.110  0.361     0.070   Clutter+0.11 House-0.11
4     r0c1     quiet        0.000  0.478     0.000   -            -

That self-diff is not a null test

Diffing an index against itself gives shift = 0 for every tile by construction — it cannot return anything but all-quiet, for any input. It pins that the arithmetic is right, which is worth having and is not evidence about real change. The real null test, named in tilechange.py, re-runs the segmenter on one date and takes the 95th percentile of the resulting shift. That has not been done, because it needs a second segmentation of the same ground.

The discount is proportional, not subtractive — a correction, not a preference. A tile flipping wholly DryGrassland → GreenGrassland has shift 0.90 and volatility 0.90; subtraction still leaves 0.225 of “excess”, enough to surface the seasons as news. Proportionally it leaves 0.09 and reads as expected.

s3_triage.compile_query already parses transitions — House -> Clutter, and “where a road was paved” inferring DirtRoad → PavedRoad. Policy.transition is populated and consumed by nothing yet. That is the hook.

Read this before you trust a number

Where the bodies are buried

Every heuristic constant is a guess

They are grouped at the top of each module, named, and tabulated in the docs with a “where this should actually come from” column. Do not treat any number the solutions produce as a finding.

The aza class mapping is suspect

Those tiles carry no ID_TO_LABEL_MAPPING tag, so they are read with the mapping from the sinai drop. Under it, “marl badlands” is the dominant class inside dense urban Gaza and roughly half of all OSM-mapped buildings have no House under them. Settle this before concluding anything from aza.

Neither aza nor sinai contains the rocks half the taxonomy describes

Three geological maps agree both are Quaternary coastal plain. leb is the first AOI that actually has them — Limestone 3.25%, Dolomite 1.01%, Nari 0.44% — so S2's UNDECIDABLE-NEEDS-geological-map will genuinely fire there, and no obtainable map answers it: the Geological Survey of Israel's service returns empty north of the border.

No DEM, anywhere

Every mean_slope and aspect_circvar is 0.0, which is a valid-looking number meaning unmeasured. The audit abstains rather than scoring against it. One 29 MB Copernicus GLO-30 tile covers all three AOIs and closes this.

Future work

What I would do next, in order

  1. Change detection next session

    The seam, the volatility baseline and the transition parser are in. What is missing is the second date and the region-level bridge to s6_change. Start with the null test on a real pair — if it is not quiet, nothing after it means anything.

  2. Wire the DEM one afternoon

    Copernicus GLO-30, one tile, no auth, no non-commercial clause. A research agent measured height error at 0.61 m over Gaza, implying a slope noise floor of 1.43° and 97–98% of tiles clearing a 3σ bar for tile-mean slope — those figures come from that survey, not from this repo, which has no DEM to check them against. Be equally clear about what it cannot do — per-post aspect clears 3σ on only a third of posts, and dip angle never does.

  3. Fill the class notes needs a domain expert

    The highest-leverage artifact in the repo is prose, and it is currently a programmer's paraphrase of a textbook. confused_with already feeds S2's shortlist; a measured confusion beats the taxonomy's guess every time.

  4. Measure one false-positive rate

    Every solution's blocking question is the same shape: S1 needs ~150 reviewed regions, S2 needs to know whether the true class is even in its shortlist, S3 needs a detector cost model. One labelled set unblocks three of them.

  5. Make the corridor noise floor relative

    CORRIDOR_MIN_AREA_M2 is an absolute 500 m² running over AOIs spanning four orders of magnitude. It is now skipped when it would drop everything, but the deeper fix — scaling it to the AOI — would change every corridor answer and wants measuring first.

  6. Retire UNDECIDABLE-NEEDS-geological-map for nari

    It is permanently unsatisfiable: nari is a surface calcrete crust overlying mapped bedrock, and querying any geological service for it returns empty at every scale. The map does split hard from soft carbonate, which is what actually controls those classes — so the abstain code wants renaming to NEEDS-hardness-class.

Adversarial review

Sixteen defects, found by attacking it

Five reviewers were pointed at this code and told to refute, per the repo's own §10 doctrine — author never sole judge. They ran the code rather than reading it. Everything below was reproduced.

Fixed

tilemap_ui.pyScript breakout via a street name. json.dumps does not escape <, and block labels are OSM name=* tags — arbitrary text from whoever last edited that street. A label of </script><img onerror=…> closed the block and ran, in a report written to disk and re-served. Found independently by two reviewers.
playground.pySilent binary corruption. data.rstrip(b"\r\n") strips a byte set: any upload whose own last bytes are 0x0A/0x0D lost them before loader.load saw it. A 9-byte payload came back 6.
osm/burn.pyEvery corridor burned half a pixel off. to_pixels returns edge coordinates; the capsule rasteriser measured from integer indices while the polygon rasteriser used +0.5 — the two disagreed with each other. A road stripe co-registered by construction reported 80% agreement. That share is the input to every S1 reference finding. Now 100%.
tilechange.pyTruncation invented transitions. Scoring a class that merely fell off the top-4 list as absent turned a four-pixel rank swap into a reported 20%-of-tile transition — 204× overstated, verdict worth-a-look. The residual mass is now recorded and the distance is an honest lower bound.
tilechange.pyThree more in the same module. The volatility prior defaulted to 0.0 — the one value s4_products names as unsafe; the structural rule was tested after the noise floor so could never fire below it (1,310 m² of new construction read quiet); and its share halved a one-sided move, making the documented 5% bar an effective 10%.
tilechange.pyAn anti-drift guard that never ran. structural_classes_from_taxonomy imported CLASS_VOLATILITY; the table is VOLATILITY. The silent fallback fired every time, called Car structural — volatility 0.8, because a parked car moving is not a change of the ground — and omitted every rock class. The docstring claimed the two could not drift apart. They already had.
osm/vectors.pyThe cache key was blind to geometry. The fingerprint hashed way ids, tags and vertex count — so a street that MOVED hashed identically and last month's block partition was served beside this month's burn.
cli.pysolve s3 --query was accepted and ignored. It answered from the built-in policy and printed that policy's own query text, actively confirming a compile that never happened. Now wired.
s3_triage.pyA saving counted over ground never searched. Measured: cost reduction 78% where the figure over units the query applies to is 11%. Both are printed now.
playground.pyFour server defects. Content-Length: -1 bypassed the upload ceiling and drained the socket; max_mpx=nan disabled the megapixel crop outright (every comparison against NaN is False); three exception paths leaked the temp dir and returned no HTTP response at all; and the progress bar ticked "burning OSM ✓", "co-registration ✓", "blocks ✓" after the fetch had failed.
class_notes.py
playground.py		Bundled files vanished outside an editable install. Both resolved via parents[2], which only holds inside the checkout — under pip install . the default class mapping and the notes silently disappeared.
tests/22 new tests. tilechange, tilemap, tilemap_ui and traversability had zero; they are now 84–96%. Suite: 180 → 202 passing.

Five questions for you

These change an interface, a stored format, or a documented number, so I have not touched them.

  1. S2 mixes two scoring scales in one ranking correctness

    reference_score returns None per candidate, so when OSM is silent about only some candidates, one ranking compares raw own against 0.7·own + 0.3·ref. Measured on a synth tile: 36 of 389 adjudications mix the two, and six candidates were penalised for having OSM support. The "bit-identical when silent" guarantee holds only when OSM is silent about every candidate. Renormalise the whole ranking when any candidate has a reference score, or gate the term on all-or-nothing? The first is more informative, the second is simpler to defend.

  2. The playground can be wedged permanently server

    A FIFO inside an uploaded directory blocks rasterio forever while holding the global lock; every later run queues behind it and only a restart recovers. Separately _JOBS never evicts and each job pins its whole rendered report — 3.2 MB measured per run, for the process lifetime. Add a job timeout and an LRU cap, or leave it as a single-user local tool and just document it?

  3. Three of four "machine-read" class-note fields have no consumer taxonomy

    Only confused_with is read. The template tells an analyst that season "feeds S6's phenology gate", never is "a candidate prior" and scale "replaces the guessed area bands in S2" — filling any of them changes nothing. Wire them, or downgrade the claim to "recorded for planned consumers"? I have downgraded the wording for now; wiring scale into S2's area bands is the cheapest real win.

  4. Nodata is scored as impassable contract

    traversability zeroes its score on invalid pixels and only says so when an explicit mask was passed — a sparse export carries valid and no mask, so nothing is said, and a half-nodata tile reads 0.256 against 0.512 over real ground. The validator also forbids non-finite values, so a provider has no per-pixel way to say "unmeasured". Add a NaN-means-unmeasured channel to the contract before your estimator lands? Easier now than after.

  5. Ship the data files inside the package packaging

    I patched the path resolution, but the real fix is to move smart_terrain_class_ids.json and class_notes.md into segmap_digest/data/ and read them with importlib.resources. That moves files the docs reference by path. Worth doing before anyone installs this non-editable?

What held up. The reviewers cleared several things by running them: WayFootprint.local_mask reproduces its bbox exactly across 441 cases at every raster edge; there is no row/col swap anywhere; every empty-input path is clean; page_results escapes every interpolation it controls; and S2 is bit-identical across 60 adjudications when OSM is silent about everything. The S1 coverage block, osm_delta, the registered=False short-circuit and S3's three-way rejection vocabulary were all called exemplary.
